chunks: From him, from Ahmad, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Ali ibn Al-Hasan ibn Ribat, from Muhammad ibn Bajil, the brother of Ali ibn Bajil, who said:

I saw Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) praying. A man passed by him while he was between the two prostrations, so Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) threw a pebble at him, and the man turned towards him.
ai.seo_question: What did the Imam do when a man passed in front of him while he was praying between the two prostrations?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* highlights the specific etiquette of *sadd al-masadd* (blocking the path) during prayer, with Imam Al-Sadiq (AS) demonstrating a practical response to a passerby interrupting his worship during the brief interval between prostrations. The incident underscores the sanctity of the prayer space and the Imam’s authority in maintaining its decorum, serving as a foundational precedent for juristic discussions on the validity of prayer when a person passes directly in front of the worshipper.
